classification.difficultyReason: Infer equal chords from equal perpendicular distances, connect them to equal central sectors, and introduce radii mentally to derive the pentagon angle from isosceles triangles.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

spec.description: An inscribed pentagon with centre O, five equal perpendicular distances from O to its sides, five right-angle squares and x inside its upper-right vertex.
spec.mathematics: All five sides are chords equidistant from the centre. Their perpendicular distances have matching single ticks. The chords and corresponding minor central angles are equal.
spec.answerVisibility: The source's printed 108° is answer evidence only; it is omitted from the question diagram.

answer.worked:
Equal perpendicular distances from the centre give equal chords. Equal chords subtend equal angles at the centre.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Each central angle}&=\frac{360^\circ}{5}\\&=72^\circ\\\text{Each base angle}&=\frac{180^\circ-72^\circ}{2}\\&=54^\circ\\x&=54^\circ+54^\circ\\&=108^\circ\end{align*}$$

The triangles formed by joining the centre to consecutive vertices are isosceles because their radii are equal.
